\begin{bankq}[id=SII04-P1-CHEM-S1-Q04, source={Score-II - Test 04 (07 May 2021)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=single, subtopic={Defects}, answer={D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S3 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: doping interstitial elements in a CCP crystal | steps: octahedral hole radius 0.414 r and tetrahedral 0.225 r; radius of M a/2; compare 0.16a and 0.25a with the hole radii; which hole each fits; choose the option}]
In an CCP crystal of metal \textbf{M} (diameter $=$ `a' \AA), we are trying to dope two smaller elements \textbf{X} (radius $=$ `0.16a' \AA) and/or \textbf{Y} (radius $=$ `0.25a' \AA) without disturbing \textbf{M-M} contact, then select correct matching.

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.46\linewidth}p{0.46\linewidth}@{}}
\textbf{OBSERVATIONS} & \textbf{REASONS}\\
(A) Octahedral voids can have both X \& Y & O-Voids are bigger than T-voids\\
(B) Density of crystal increases on adding X & X atoms are heavier than M atoms and size of Unit cell remains same\\
(C) Packing Fraction remains same on adding X & Dimensions of unit cell remain same\\
(D) Tetrahedral Void can't have either X or Y & $\dfrac{r_X}{r_M}=0.32>$ Radius ratio of ideal Tetrahedral void\\
\end{tabular}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\end{center}
\end{bankq}

(v) Co-ordination number of X with respect of Z in the lattice is 8\par
(vi) Co-ordination number of X with respect of Y in the lattice is 6\par
(vii) Number of next nearest neighbour of Y is 8\par
(viii) If edge length of $\frac18$th equal part of the isolated unit cell is b, then the minimum distance between two Y atoms would be $\sqrt2\,$b
\end{bankq}
